questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.**

Tourists visiting Leh take home photos and memories but __leave back__ a mountain of waste.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e leave behind.

 Some **verbs** are followed by a particular **preposition,** which changes its meaning, known as **phrasal verbs.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/39a99fb58c390735920110d1e3d11e27b20401fcd8fd45c9d2318a72ac140c52.png] 

__
 
• But not all **prepositions** form meaningful **phrasal verbs.**
 
• For example:
 
 
• *My parents were **let over** by me. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *My parents were** let down** by me. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
• In the example given above, **'let over'** isn't a** phrasal verb **whereas **'let down' means to disappoint someone.**
 
 
 
• **​**In the given question, only **'leave behind'** is a phrasal verb which means **to go away and not take something or someone with you.**
 
• **The rest of the options **don't add up.

Correct Sentence__: *"Tourists visiting Leh take home photos and memories but **__leave behind__ **a mountain of waste."*

questions.question:
Directions: **From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

I said you to prepare the article yesterday but you didn’t.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2) i.e I said you.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52da89e0a2679b367562ad6c0d6e656a668762aeb60deda63544b7552771e3b0.png] The verb **'said'** is used in the following forms given below:

__
 
• It's used in case of **direct speech** in the narration.
 
• **'said to'** is always followed by another **subject or object.**
 
• In the** indirect **speech of narration,** 'said to'** is converted into** 'told'.**
 
• If any **object** is not given in the sentence, the verb **'said'** is followed by the conjunction **'that'.**
 
• For example:
 
 
• **Indirect speech- ​***He **said to** me, "You are a fool."*
 
• **Direct speech- ***He **told** me that I was a fool.*
 
 
 
• The given sentence is in the **indirect** speech of narration, hence the verb **'said'** will be replaced by **'told'.**

**Correct sentence**__**: ***"I **told **you to prepare the article yesterday but you didn’t."*

questions.question:
Directions: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

You can visit me on .......... at 7 o’clock.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e Sunday.

 *​*There are certain **phrases/nouns** which are not **preceded** by a **preposition**, especially **'on'.***

__
 
• Some of them are given below:
 
 
• **today, tomorrow, yesterday, the next day/month/year, tonight, last night,** etc.
 
 
 
• Though there are some **nouns/phrases** which can be **preceded **by the preposition** 'on':**
 
 
• **​Exact time in terms of a day or a particular date.**
 
• **Monday, 7th May, Thursday, 12th July, etc.**
 
 
 
• For example:​*
 
 
• *I met her** on last Saturday. ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *I met her **last Saturday.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
 

 
• Since the given blank is preceded by the preposition** 'on',** only** 'Sunday' **will fulfill the desired purpose.

Correct Sentence__: *"You can visit me on __**Sunday**__ at 7 o’clock."*

questions.question: **Select the most appropriate option that will fill in the blank number 2.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e 'agony'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Agony- extreme physical or mental suffering.
 
• The term '**Agony**' accurately conveys the extreme mental and emotional suffering that the Maratha chiefs would have experienced due to the loss of their freedom.
 
• 'Agony' indicates a greater intensity of suffering compared to '**Distress**', reflecting the profound impact of losing independence, which aligns with their desperation to regain it.
 
• Understanding the depth of suffering experienced by the Maratha chiefs, 'Agony' is indeed an appropriate choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Agony'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• distress- extreme anxiety, sorrow, or pain.
 
• fear- an unpleasant emotion caused by the threat of danger, pain, or harm.
 
• depression- feelings of severe despondency and dejection.
 
• While 'Fear' and 'Depression' are **emotions**, they do not specifically highlight the **severity of the stress** caused by loss of freedom as 'Agony' does.
